⚠️Heavy rainfall and blustery winds will continue over the northern Phillipines until mid Monday morning⚠️
(11:00 Sun, Oct 19th, PHT) 
Hazards: 
• Additional rainfall amounts ranging 50 to 100 mm, except 150 mm locally. 
• Winds gusting to 90km/h locally along the northeastern shores

Tropical storm Fengshen is currently located over Manila, Philippines and is bringing torrential rainfall to parts of the region. 
Fengshen is forecast to travel northwest over the next 48 hours, emerging from the Philippines in 10 to 12 hours. 

The system is expected to intensify considerably after leaving the Philippines, and is expected to max out in intensity late Tuesday as a T4 typhoon with sustained winds ranging 130 to 145km/h, well off-shore of Guangdong China. 
However, a powerful cold front will slam into the typhoon on Wednesday, pushing cold dry air into the core, which is expected to inevitably result in a weakening trend as the system veers southwest. 
Throughout the reminder of the week, Fengshen will travel southwest towards Vietnam, and is expected to weaken to a tropical storm or remnant low before making landfall. 

Stay tuned for updates! 
#TyphoonFengshen #Tropicalstorm #Fengshen #Phillipines #Flooding

Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 5 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Tropical Storm RAMIL
Issued at: 11:00 AM, 19 October 2025(Sunday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, Cavite, Batangas, Laguna, Quezon, Bulacan(Dona Remedios Trinidad, San Miguel, Norzagaray), Rizal(Jala-Jala, Pililla, Tanay, Binangonan, Cardona, Morong, Baras) and Zambales(Candelaria, Santa Cruz, Masinloc).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Pampanga, Metro Manila, Bataan, Rizal(Antipolo, Rodriguez, San Mateo, Angono, Cainta, Taytay, Teresa), Bulacan(Angat, Bustos, Baliuag, San Rafael, San Ildefonso, Balagtas, Bocaue, Bulakan, Calumpit, Malolos, Meycauayan, San Jose del Monte, Guiguinto, Hagonoy, Marilao, Obando, Pandi, Paombong, Plaridel, Pulilan, Santa Maria) and Zambales(Olongapo, Subic, Botolan, San Marcelino, Cabangan, Iba, Palauig, Castillejos, San Antonio, San Felipe, San Narciso) which may persist within 3 hours.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 2:00 PM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.
